text:
on a painful topic

watching ur library and bookshelves dwindle as u give away, donate, and gift ur old books en masse

empty shelves --> mixed emotions, like larry wildman...

but it is necessary and recommended

considerations:

1/6

a library is aesthetically pleasing but it’s almost entirely vanity/ego/bullshit/outer scorecard.

those books could be in the possession of someone younger who hasnt yet read them

as u know, a single book can permanently change someone's life.

or, they can sit on ur shelves collecting dust...and why? 

so that ppl can perceive u in a certain light? is ur goal to be judged not by who u are, but by ur bookshelf?

if u are well-read, that is going to come out in how u think, speak, and write.

2/6

how often do u see a video of some dude with a massive floor-to-ceiling collection behind his desk, and u can tell from how he talks that he hasnt touched a single one of them.

like...those spines are looking CRISPY, brotha...entire collection would qualify as fresh-out-the-box AM95 levels of deadstock

the party line is prob "oh its better to have them and not need them," or something about viewing books like medicine at a hospital, but u just know its garbage.

3/6

reading Will Durant's "Story of Civilization" series -- which is 11 hardcovers, about 800-1000 pages each, whole set some ~18 inches wide -- took me close to five years.

with intense focus and no straying, I maybe, maybe could've done it in somewhere between two and three.

point being...when I see a bookshelf that has 100x this amount of pages on it, and not Grisham novels, but thick reading, history, biography, philosophy, academia, etc...I know that at least 99% of those are unread.

I’m not a prick about this but within 1-2 questions u could easily get the “oh yea I didn’t actually read that” out of someone -- about some book(s) they keep directly behind them on camera

then u just look like a real doofus with a collection assembled purely for affectation.

come on dog...that Spengler, that Milton, we all know those are unreadable...u dont have to keep pump faking.

4/6

personally...at this point, I have no use for a book that isnt uploaded to my brain.

I need that info on instant recall. I need it to help me navigate life. I don't read for any other reason.

if its anything factual, LLM's have almost entirely killed the need for "let me grab xyz off the shelf and check."

additionally, any book over 95 years old becomes public domain and is free on gutenberg/archive. all my favorite titles are over 95 years old.

plus, every time I move, the majority of my boxes are for books. this feels increasingly silly.

5/6

I'm trying to get down to just 2-3 shelves of books,  personal favorites, ones that I have re-read multiple times and will do so again in the future.

the way I've determined which these are, is that I'll mail a copy to a friend, then a few weeks later reach for it and realize its not there. 

usually these are old books but ones published less than 95 years ago - maybe a modern translation, a compilation or "collected works," a Portable, something like that.

in any case, its a very, very small subset of your total books; the books u miss upon noticing that they're gone. 

6/6

the vast majority, u know just looking at them: "I'm never reading that book again."

unless ur willing to admit "I'm insecure and trying to impress people who come over," u got no need for those titles.

a single good book can change a motherfucker's life. u know this, I know this.

pass 'em along, hermano...don't be a hoarder

"greatest gift you can give is to help another man think differently" 🙏
